Scope, status labels and source qualityThis is a curated directory, not an exhaustive index of the internet and not a live market-data terminal. Every link is an entry point to a source, not a guarantee of data quality, pricing, India eligibility or trading access. “Public research” means informational access—not permission to trade a product. “Explicitly blocked” is used only where a specific public restriction is documented; “Eligibility not verified” means do not assume real-money access is permitted; “Legal/regulatory reference” denotes a law or warning page, not a blocked website. Social posts, rumours and third-party allegations are leads only: verify against original filings, exchange releases, regulator notices or methodology documents. The directory intentionally excludes stolen credential dumps, hacked private databases and instructions for bypassing platform restrictions.

Compare methodologies on the same instrument

Run more than one framework to expose disagreement. The methods below are search lenses; they do not all have equal evidential support. Astrology and unsupported cycle claims should be kept separate from testable price, fundamental and statistical evidence.

X accounts and public analysis feeds to investigate

03 / Follow the information flow

News, Social Signals & Market-Move Radar

A workflow for finding fast-moving narratives, verifying catalysts and separating real information from hype.

Important: This page does not know which asset will pump or dump today. There is no reliable source that guarantees daily, weekly, monthly or yearly direction. Use the following resources to build evidence-based scenarios; treat unverified social posts, paid “insider” tips and sudden microcap/token promotions as potential manipulation risks.

Quick-launch news searches

Global market headlines ↗Fed / CPI / yields ↗Gold / XAUUSD ↗Forex / central banks ↗Oil / inventories ↗Crypto listings / exploits ↗Search X for breaking finance ↗Google Trends ↗

1. Primary-source events

First, confirm what actually happened. Check filings, exchange notices, company investor-relations releases, central banks, regulators and official data calendars.

  • SEC / NSE / BSE disclosures
  • Company earnings, guidance, deals and recalls
  • Fed / BLS / BEA / EIA releases
Open SEC filings ↗

2. News propagation

Use wire feeds and aggregators to notice how a story spreads. Deduplicate repeated headlines and preserve the earliest publication time.

  • Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, FT
  • GDELT, Google News RSS, financial APIs
  • Record updates/corrections separately
Open GDELT ↗

3. Crowd attention

Search interest, X, Reddit and ticker communities can reveal attention spikes—but can also be noisy, botted or coordinated.

  • Mentions vs 7/30-day baseline
  • Distinct credible sources vs reposts
  • Source identity and original citation
Open Trends ↗

4. Market confirmation

Look for price and volume behaviour after the event rather than assuming a headline predicts direction.

  • Relative volume and spread
  • Breakout/failed breakout context
  • Related assets and broad-market direction
Open Stock Screener ↗

5. Positioning / derivatives

Use options volume, open interest, COT, ETF flows and funding as supporting evidence. Each data series has its own reporting lag.

  • Volume is not the same as opening positions
  • Options can be hedges or multi-leg trades
  • Delayed reports are not live order flow
Open Cboe statistics ↗

6. Manipulation / risk check

Before interpreting a fast move, investigate liquidity, ownership concentration, contract controls and whether the promotion itself is the catalyst.

  • Thin books, sudden paid boosts
  • Unusual holder clusters or unlocks
  • Unverified “guaranteed pump” claims
Pump-and-dump warning ↗

04 / Short to long horizon

Daily, Weekly, Monthly & Yearly Scenario Research

Use different inputs for different horizons. A 5-minute volume spike should not be used as a yearly thesis.

INTRADAY / DAILY

What may move today?

  • Economic release / earnings / official event calendar
  • Premarket or session gap and relative volume
  • Current trend, spread, liquidity and volatility
  • Freshness of headline and reaction after publication

Useful links: Calendar · Screener · Movers

WEEKLY

What may trend this week?

  • Next-week central-bank and macro events
  • Weekly structure and sector/asset relative strength
  • COT positioning, ETF flows and investor sentiment
  • Upcoming earnings, unlocks and known catalysts

Useful links: COT · AAII · BTC ETF flows

MONTHLY

What may lead over a month?

  • Earnings estimates/revisions and guidance
  • Rate/yield/FX regime and liquidity context
  • Monthly trend, breadth, industry relative strength
  • Fund flows, expiry/rolls, rebalancing and supply events

Useful links: Analyst ratings · Macro forecasts · ETF flows

QUARTERLY / YEARLY

What may shape a long-term thesis?

  • Growth, inflation, policy and debt cycle
  • Company fundamentals, valuation and cash flow
  • Long-run supply/demand, capex, inventory and technology
  • Scenario range, assumptions and forecast revisions

Useful links: IMF WEO · BlackRock BII · Vanguard outlook

How to interpret forecast sources

Tier A — Primary facts

Company filings, exchange announcements, regulator notices, central banks and official data releases. Use these to confirm what happened.

Tier B — High-quality reporting and data providers

Established newswires, financial data APIs, exchange analytics and analyst consensus. Check timestamps, methodology, rights and whether the item is preliminary/corrected.

Tier C — Social, community and “whale” accounts

Use as leads only. Require evidence, source diversity and price/volume confirmation. A rumour with high engagement is not equivalent to a verified catalyst.

Forecast discipline: daily/weekly market direction is inherently uncertain. Store forecast issuer, horizon, publication date, target/range, key assumptions and later outcome. Track calibration and error over time rather than selecting the loudest forecast. Never present a sentiment score, analyst price target, backtest or AI output as guaranteed.

How to use public disclosures, insider activity and leak reporting

Use SEC Form 4/13F, exchange filings, court records, sanctions and published investigative reporting as evidence-backed research inputs. Disclosed insider transactions are retrospective, and institutional holdings often have reporting lags. A person’s or company’s appearance in an offshore-leak dataset does not by itself establish wrongdoing. Do not trade on material non-public information or rely on paid “leak” groups without independently verifiable evidence.

What the India filters do—and do not—mean
  • Public research: a public information/data source; not a declaration that a related product is legally tradeable in India.
  • Explicitly blocked: the directory has a specific restriction reference; do not bypass it.
  • Eligibility not verified: platform/country rules or Indian legal clearance are not established in this directory.
  • Legal/regulatory reference: official laws, warnings or regulator pages for checking the rules.

For product-specific advice, check the current primary regulator/exchange source and obtain qualified legal advice where necessary.

Market data and API integration: key fields to store

For each feed, store source URL, instrument identifier, exchange/venue, currency, unit, contract multiplier, trading hours, last trade/quote timestamp, retrieval timestamp, time zone, latency class, licensing/redistribution rights, missing-data flags and provider status. For event/news records store publication time, event time, original source, update/correction time, entities/assets affected and confidence/evidence notes. These fields prevent stale data from being misread as current intelligence.
